- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially >0.75) — model tends to overshoot in bullish sentiment phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (especially <0.3) — model shows reluctance to drop below recent lows.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays reacting to recent price drops or sentiment shifts — especially in the first 5–7 days of forecast horizon.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights short-term volatility and underweights long-term trend — tends to overreact to recent spikes and underreact to sustained declines.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate mid-term price peaks (especially 10–15 day horizon) and underestimate troughs — sentiment history should be weighted more heavily in early forecast days.
- Sentiment decay effect: model ignores sentiment decay after 3–5 days — if sentiment peaks then drops, model holds high forecast for longer than actual price correction.
